chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated that his father, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ziyad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Thabit ibn Dinar, from the Master of the Worshippers Ali ibn al-Husayn, from the Master of the Martyrs al-Husayn ibn Ali, from the Master of the Trustees, the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them all)

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said to me: 'The Imams after me are twelve, the first of them is you, O Ali, and the last of them is the Riser (al-Qa'im) upon whose hands God - blessed and exalted is His mention - will open the easts and wests of the earth.'

key_terms.مَشَارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغَارِبَهَا: The easts and wests of the earth

ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve Imams according to this hadith from Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith serves as a foundational proof for the number and lineage of the Twelve Imams, explicitly linking the Imamate to Ali ibn Abi Talib and culminating in al-Qa'im. The mention of opening the 'east and west' underscores the global scope of the Mahdi's justice, a theme deeply resonant with Shia eschatology and the universal application of divine authority.
